blocks.heading: Canada Has the Clearer

figures.label: Living-Cost Coverage Period
figures.source: Germany is dramatically cheaper on tuition: most public universities charge zero tuition, only a semester contribution of roughly EUR 150-350, though a few institutions such as TU Munich and universities in Baden-Wurttemberg now charge non-EU students separately. Add blocked-account living funds of about EUR 11,208 for the visa plus 12-24 months of actual living costs, and a 2-year German masters commonly lands well under Rs 25-30 lakh total. Canada runs higher: total 2-year cost typically falls between roughly Rs 28-38 lakh at accessible universities and Rs 60-77 lakh at premium ones like the University of Toronto, once tuition and living costs are both counted.
figures.text: Add blocked-account living funds of about EUR 11,208 for the visa plus 12-24 months of actual living costs, and a 2-year German masters commonly lands well under Rs 25-30 lakh total.

Add blocked-account living funds of about EUR 11,208 for the visa plus 12-24 months of actual living costs, and a 2-year German masters commonly lands well under Rs 25-30 lakh total. Canada runs higher: total 2-year cost typically falls between roughly Rs 28-38 lakh at accessible universities and Rs 60-77 lakh at premium ones like the University of Toronto, once tuition and living costs are both counted.

figures.label: PR Eligibility Timeline
figures.source: Germany can also lead to permanent residence, sometimes faster in raw months (21 months with B1 German under the EU Blue Card route), but that timeline assumes you already speak German at a working level and land a Blue Card-eligible role, which is a real hurdle for most fresh Indian postgraduates outside big cities and large employers.

blocks.heading: Language and Cultural Adjustment

items.text: English is the working language almost everywhere outside Quebec, so day-to-day life, job interviews, and networking do not require a second language.
A large existing Indian community across Toronto, Vancouver, and other cities means familiar food, festivals, and social groups are easy to find from day one.

The main adjustment cost is financial: higher rent, higher cost of living in the cities where most jobs concentrate, and a currency gap that makes even entry-level salaries feel tight against Canadian living costs at first.
